lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4 you met inventors of the past. What did James Watt improve in 1769? (The steam engine.) Today: two famous design movements, and the ideas behind them.
The Arts and Crafts movement began in Britain in the late 1800s. Its designers disliked cheap, badly made factory goods, and wanted beautiful things made by hand by skilled craftspeople.

William Morris (1834 to 1896) led it. His wallpapers and fabrics have patterns of leaves, flowers and birds. He said: 'Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be beautiful.'
Arts and Crafts furniture used natural materials like oak, simple, honest shapes and joints you can see. It often had carved or painted decoration, inspired by nature and medieval crafts.
The Bauhaus was a school of art and design in Germany, started in 1919 by the architect Walter Gropius. It moved from Weimar to Dessau in 1925, then to Berlin, and closed in 1933.
Bauhaus designers used simple geometric shapes, primary colours and new materials like tubular steel. They designed for factories, so good things could be made for many people.
'Form follows function': a thing's shape should come from its job. The American architect Louis Sullivan wrote 'form ever follows function' in 1896, and Bauhaus designers took up the idea.

Try it in the world: build two rooms side by side: one Arts and Crafts (oak and leafy patterns), one Bauhaus (steel, circles, squares and triangles). For real: find a chair or a pattern at home and decide which it is closer to. Next: projects.

exercises.prompt: Which movement does this pattern belong to?
exercises.hint: Leaves and flowers, or circles and squares?
exercises.explain: Arts and Crafts: a handmade pattern of leaves and flowers.

exercises.prompt: Arts and Crafts designers liked things made by hand.
exercises.hint: What did they dislike about factory goods?
exercises.explain: True: they valued the skill of craftspeople.

exercises.prompt: In which country was the Bauhaus?
exercises.hint: Weimar, Dessau and Berlin are its cities.
exercises.explain: Germany: in Weimar, then Dessau, then Berlin.

exercises.prompt: Which movement is this chair from?
exercises.explain: Bauhaus: a simple chair of bent steel tube, made in a factory.

exercises.hint: Handmade and natural, or machine-made and geometric?
exercises.explain: Arts and Crafts: handmade, leafy patterns, oak and wool. Bauhaus: factories, simple shapes, tubular steel.

exercises.prompt: The Bauhaus opened in 1919 and closed in 1933. For how many years was it open?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.
Form is shape; function is the job.
choices: a thing's shape should come from its job
exercises.explain: The shape should come from what the thing has to do.

exercises.prompt: Match each person to what they did.
exercises.hint: One led Arts and Crafts; one started a school; one was an American architect; one bent steel tube.
exercises.explain: Morris: leafy wallpapers. Gropius: the Bauhaus. Sullivan: 'form ever follows function'. Breuer: a tubular steel chair.

exercises.hint: Look for simple shapes and no decoration.
exercises.explain: The one with a round base, a straight stem and a plain dome.

exercises.prompt: Bauhaus designers wanted their designs made in factories, so many people could have them.
exercises.explain: True: good design for everyone, made by machines.

exercises.prompt: William Morris was born in 1834 and died in 1896. How old was he when he died?
exercises.hint: Take the birth year from the year he died.

exercises.prompt: Morris said: 'Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be…'
exercises.hint: He loved things that were both useful and lovely to look at.
exercises.explain: Beautiful: useful or beautiful, and best of all both.

exercises.prompt: A lamp has a glass disc base, a straight steel stem and a plain round shade. Whose ideas are these?
exercises.hint: Simple shapes, new materials, no decoration.
exercises.explain: The Bauhaus: simple geometric shapes, and form following function.

items: the first Arts and Crafts exhibition (1888)

exercises.prompt: Why did Arts and Crafts designers dislike many factory goods of their time?
choices: they were often cheap and badly made
exercises.explain: Many were cheap and badly made, so they wanted skilled, careful handwork.

exercises.prompt: Both movements cared about how well a thing does its job.
exercises.hint: Morris wanted useful things; the Bauhaus wanted form to follow function.
exercises.explain: True: both cared about usefulness, though they made things in very different ways.
